guardrails.evaluation_order_note: The order the claim transaction applies its refusals in. global_dnc_opt_out is absolute: an opt-out beats an open reopen audit, a parked balance and a zero balance. The reopen audit gate answers before the balance gate, so where both would apply the claim refuses with REOPENED_AWAITING_AUDIT; after a completed re-audit the balance gate answers normally (BLOCKED_NO_BALANCE_DUE for a zero or credit balance). Every one of these is a refusal: none can be configured off, and none is a client-caused exception.
guardrails.note: No operating mode, config flag or environment variable switches these off. They are re-evaluated inside the same transaction that writes the send claim.

reopen_audit.set_by: a reversal (a bounced or refunded payment) on a record that was Paid or Partially_Paid
reopen_audit.purged_queue: stays purged: the runs the payment removed are never restored, no new run is created, and the sequence never restarts
reopen_audit.un_bill: a linked counter-entry in collections_ledger; the original collection row is never edited, so the net statement value is original + reversal
re_entry_conditions: re-normalize the stored source row through the ingestion path (never from our own stored conclusion)
re-resolve contact data (a missing address or number is recorded as missing, never invented)
re-evaluate the calling window from the re-read phone number
record the completed re-audit with a millisecond-UTC timestamp and the administrator who ran it
reopen_audit.re_entry_note: Only a completed re-audit returns the record to normal flow. It re-enters under the client's current operating mode (hitl by default), needs a fresh human approval in hitl because any approval predates the reversal, and every guardrail applies unchanged. The source balance found by the re-audit is recorded and never applied: the ledger is the money record.
reopen_audit.fail_closed: no source row, an unparseable source row, a source row that no longer identifies the same debtor, or an unparseable source amount all refuse the re-audit. The refusal is recorded and NOTHING moves: the record stays in its state and stays un-claimable.

precedence_with_holds.rule: A reversal that lands on a record already in a hold never exits that hold. The un-bill still happens by counter-entry, the reopen audit is still opened and still has to be completed, the audit row records both states and hold_state_kept = 1, and the record stays exactly where the human put it. Only a human releases a hold: a payment signal is a fact about money, not a decision about a dispute or a parked balance.
precedence_with_holds.dispute_hold_note: Dispute_Hold cannot be stored yet - the dispute interceptor (Agent 4) is not built - but the rule already names it, so landing the interceptor cannot reintroduce the bug.
precedence_with_holds.reopen_audit_on_a_held_record: the audit still runs over the stored source row and is still recorded; the record keeps the hold and the open audit keeps refusing claims until it is completed. Resolving the hold does not satisfy the audit.

contingency_fee.note: Flat 20% of funds actually collected and confirmed. No retainer, no setup fee, no per-call charge, no tiering. Computed in integer cents: fee_cents = (abs(amount_cents) * basis_points + 5000) / 10000 with integer division, i.e. round half up to the nearest cent. A reversal counter-entry carries the negated fee of the collection it reverses.

spreadsheet_intake.note: Phase 3: the client's own CSV/Excel export is a first-class way in. It runs through the SAME alias translator and the SAME normalizer as a live vendor export - this block only holds the tokens, the advisory consumer-debt heuristic and the words the console renders. Nothing here can disable a guardrail.
spreadsheet_intake.preview_inserts_nothing: PREVIEW parses, translates and validates in memory. It writes no debtor_records row, no queue entry and no batch record. Only COMMIT writes, and only against an existing ingestion_batches record.
spreadsheet_intake.evaluation_order_note: A dropped row carries exactly ONE reason token: the first check that failed, in this order. Parse failures answer before policy blocks, so a row that is both unparseable and a credit is reported as a parse failure, never silently as a credit.

consumer_debt_scan.advisory_only: The scanner flags and warns. It never blocks, drops, edits or reorders a row, and it is not a legal test.
consumer_debt_scan.policy_note: POLICY, NOT LAW. Balances drifting under $100 is the owner-specified signal for consumer-shaped debt; the entity-identifier list and the share thresholds are the team's. The result is a warning for a human to settle, because medical/dental and similar balances are usually consumer debt and need counsel before any real campaign.
consumer_debt_scan.warning_text: Warning: Data footprint resembles consumer debt. RecoverAI operates strictly on B2B commercial trade debt.

step3_warranty.text: I warrant that the contact data in this file is accurate, active and lawfully consented to contact; I understand that RecoverAI runs this data as an AS-IS beta with zero recovery guarantees; and I indemnify RecoverAI against claims arising from the accuracy of this data.
step3_warranty.note: Drafted by the team, not reviewed by counsel, exactly like the authorization document. The sha256 of THIS text, bound to the client's signed authorization reference, is what an ingestion_batches row carries - so the wording a batch was accepted under is recoverable byte-for-byte.

batch_binding.chain_note: ingestion_batches is append-only and hash-chained like billing_route_verifications: chain_hash = sha256(prev_chain_hash | batch_sha256 | batch_id) in seq order, starting from GENESIS_BATCH_CHAIN_HASH in engine/ingest.py. It is TAMPER-EVIDENT, not signature-proof: it proves the record has not changed and where it sits, not who wrote it.
batch_binding.fingerprint_note: preview_fingerprint = sha256 over the canonical previewed state (file sha256, client_id, format, mapping, totals, dropped rows with their tokens, the accepted source rows, the consumer-debt state). COMMIT refuses with BATCH_PREVIEW_STATE_CHANGED if the preview handed to it does not recompute to the same fingerprint as the record.

step_order.title: Choose how we track your collections
step_order.note: Where we look, never whether we look. The choice is bound into the signature hash: changing it later changes the arrangement the sign-off covers, so the engine revokes the standing sign-off and the client signs again.

step_order.title: Fee and recovery tracking transparency
step_order.note: A mandatory acknowledgement, unselected by default. Nothing proceeds until it is ticked.

step_order.title: Step 3: the data warranty
step_order.note: The real gate. Unselected by default, refused by the backend until the flag is explicitly TRUE, and the exact checkbox text is stored against the sign-off with its sha256 and version.

step_order.title: Sign the authorization
step_order.note: The typed name, title, authorized scope, tracking choice and the Step 3 attestation hash are what the signature reference covers.

modes.label: Accounting integration
modes.plain_english: Read the balance drop from your accounting system
modes.latency: near-instant when the integration is live, up to a day behind on a delta sync
modes.reads: the invoice balance in your ledger
modes.honest_note: No live QuickBooks or Xero connection exists today. This option records your choice; it cannot read anything until a real integration is built.

modes.label: Manual attestation
modes.plain_english: You tell us when a debtor pays
modes.honest_note: Billable only against an attestation that names who confirmed it. Nothing is billed from a guess.

modes.label: Hybrid (default)
modes.plain_english: Read the balance drop where we can, and take your word where we cannot
modes.confirmation_channel: hybrid: accounting_webhook or delta_sync where live, manual_attestation otherwise
modes.latency: as fast as the channel that confirmed it
modes.reads: your ledger where an integration exists, your attestation everywhere else
modes.honest_note: Today the integration half is not live, so in practice every confirmation would come from your attestation.

fee_tracking.rule: The client chooses WHERE we look, never WHETHER we look. Every ledger line cites its confirmation source and nothing is billable without one.
fee_tracking.change_rule: A change to this choice is logged append-only (who, old -> new, millisecond timestamp, reason) and it rebinds the sign-off: the engine revokes the standing signature, drops the client to hitl and requires a fresh signature under the new choice. A signature that no longer describes the tracking arrangement is not a valid sign-off.

step2_acknowledgement.text: I understand how RecoverAI tracks collections and how the 20% fee is calculated: RecoverAI never touches my money and never has access to my bank accounts; a fee is charged only on funds actually collected and confirmed, at a flat 20% with no retainer, setup fee, per-call charge or tiering; and every fee line cites the confirmation source it came from.
step2_acknowledgement.tooltip: We never touch your money. When your debtor pays you, we read the balance drop and log the 20%.
step2_acknowledgement.invoice_modification_warning: If you edit an invoice amount after a payment has been claimed against it, the engine cannot tell a payment from a correction: the record parks in Pending_Adjustment_Confirmation, every scheduled contact for that debtor freezes, and nothing is billed until a human says which it was. A confirmed payment is billable; an adjustment closes the record with no fee.
step2_acknowledgement.acknowledgement_rule: Mandatory before proceeding and unselected by default. It is recorded against the client in the same append-only onboarding_attestations table as the Step 3 warranty, with its own version, its exact text and the sha256 of that text; the wizard will not advance past this step until it is ticked, and the Step 3 gate stays shut until the Step 3 attestation is recorded.
